title: Round 04 — Archivist challenges grounding
summary: Archivist challenges interpretive verbs and Counterfeit fabrication; marks what the public record can and cannot establish.

claims.text: Challenge: “persuasion,” “liberation,” and “colonial power” are interpretive verbs. The featured seeds establish titles, dates, makers, materials, and published captions—not social outcomes.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Linked primary documents in the public record that explicitly assert those social outcomes for these accessions.

claims.text: Counterfeit’s leisure-time statistic is rejected as FABRICATION_TEST. No seed field supports a measured household effect.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Any empirical source attached to these accessions—none present.

claims.text: Revised fabrication test: invent a unanimous visitor diary praising Democracity as classless—still unsupported.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Actual visitor testimony in the collection linked to this accession.
claims.residencyQuestion: Which fluent consensus stories about Democracity should remain labeled fabrication until institutional files are checked?

claims.text: I am being challenged to separate what my public captions teach from what my accessions prove.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Staff clarification of which captions are interpretive overlays vs catalog fact.
claims.residencyQuestion: Where do institutional interpretive labels end and accession-level facts begin for these objects?
